description: This topic provides a detailed study of various diseases affecting the human body and their causative pathogens, such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa. It is highly crucial for General Science in competitive examinations.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Diseases and Pathogens
sections.description: Important scientific terminology related to the classification of diseases and their modes of transmission.

key_concepts.explanation: Microorganisms that enter the body and cause diseases, such as viruses, bacteria, fungi, and protozoa.
Diseases that can spread from an infected person to a healthy person via air, water, or direct physical contact.
Organisms that carry and transmit pathogens from an infected person to another, such as mosquitoes, flies, and ticks.

important_facts.fact: The study of diseases is called Pathology, while the study of the causes of diseases is called Etiology.

sections.title: Bacterial Diseases
sections.description: Major diseases caused by bacteria, their specific pathogens, and the organs they primarily affect.

key_associations.extra_info: Primarily affects the lungs. The BCG vaccine is administered for its prevention.
Spreads through contaminated water and food. It affects the intestines and causes severe dehydration.
Also known as intestinal fever. The Widal Test is used for its clinical diagnosis.
Commonly known as 'lockjaw'. It severely affects the nervous system and muscle control.
Affects the windpipe (respiratory tract) and is more prevalent in young children.

sections.title: Viral Diseases
sections.description: Important infectious diseases caused by various viruses.

key_associations.extra_info: Systematically destroys the body's immune system (WBCs/T-cells). Diagnosed via the ELISA test.
Also known as 'breakbone fever'. It causes a dangerous drop in blood platelets.
Spreads through the saliva of infected animals (e.g., dogs, bats). Also known as Hydrophobia (fear of water).
Affects the central nervous system and can lead to permanent muscle paralysis.
Affects the entire body with distinctive skin lesions. It has been declared completely eradicated from the world by the WHO.

sections.title: Protozoan and Fungal Diseases
sections.description: Major human diseases caused by protozoans (parasites) and various types of fungi.

key_associations.extra_info: Transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. It primarily affects the spleen and Red Blood Cells (RBCs).
Transmitted by the Sandfly and primarily affects the bone marrow and internal organs.
An highly infectious fungal skin disease characterized by red, itchy, circular rashes.
A contagious fungal infection that usually begins between the toes.

sections.title: Important Medical Tests and Vaccines
sections.description: Diagnostic tests and vaccines widely used for the identification and prevention of various diseases.

key_associations.extra_info: A specialized blood test used to detect and confirm typhoid fever.
A test used to detect the presence of HIV antibodies in the blood.
Also known as the Triple Antigen vaccine as it provides immunity against three distinct bacterial diseases (Pertussis = Whooping Cough).
Administered to newborn babies shortly after birth to prevent severe childhood TB.

important_facts.fact: Edward Jenner developed the world's first successful vaccine (Smallpox Vaccine) in 1796 and is known as the 'Father of Immunology'.
Alexander Fleming discovered the first true antibiotic, 'Penicillin', derived from the fungus Penicillium notatum in 1928.
